newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on Tuesday on short-covering, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,200 yuan (2,796$) per tonne, rising 230 yuan.
It opened at 23,040 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 23,000 and a high of 23,250.
May rose 150 to 23,250, June 210 to 23,240, July 270 to 23,240, September 220 to 23,160 and October 140 to 23,140.
Combined volume rose to 36,500 tonnes from 19,250.
Copper opened slightly up and rose steadily for most of the session with some contracts closing at their intra-day highs.
Traders said strong world market and domestic physical copper prices supported the Shanghai futures contracts, triggering short-covering.
"Improved cofidence of long position holders, boosted by the recent performance of the London Metal Exchange, was partly responsible for today's gains," one trader said.
"Firm home physical prices have made investors believe futures will not fall sharply in the short-term, triggering short-covering," he added.
Physical copper prices rose an average of around 100 yuan to 23,300 yuan on Tuesday in the Shanghai area, traders said.
But some traders said further rises of copper futures would meet strong resistance at high levels due to selling by hedgers.
"There is likely to be another chance for producers to build large short positions above the 23,500 yuan level," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected copper to move around the 23,000 yuan level in the short term.
Aluminium ended mixed. May rose 20 to 15,160, June 110 to 15,400 and July fell 100 to 15,500.
Combined volume fell to 760 tonnes from 2,080.
